vectors.name: formats-oml/basic/date-shaped-string-stays-quoted-on-write
vectors.comment: A string-kinded value that happens to be date-shaped MUST stay quoted -- writing it bare would produce a different Document on re-read (a genuine temporal literal, ch.4's grammar), silently changing its kind. Confirmed live against the reference implementation. Filed as omnist-spec#33 after this exact case was found unquoted (a real bug, not a permitted divergence) in omnist-rs, where it was fixed.

vectors.name: formats-oml/basic/genuine-date-writes-bare
vectors.comment: The companion case: a genuinely date-kinded scalar (e.g. from a schema-directed materialize, or read from a native temporal literal in another format) writes bare, no quotes -- this is the behavior formats-oml/basic/date-shaped-string-stays-quoted-on-write must NOT produce for a plain string. Confirmed live: reading a native OML date literal and writing it back stays bare.

vectors.name: formats-oml/canonical-output/repeated-labels-never-array-sugar
vectors.comment: Sec4.9: array sugar and repeated labels denote the same Document (Sec4.3.1 expands [...] at parse time), so a canonical form has to choose one, and it chooses repeated labels. A writer emitting `b: [1, 2, 3]` here produces an equal Document on re-read but different bytes, which Sec9.2 forbids for canonical output. Emitting sugar remains a legal non-canonical writer option; this vector pins what canonical means, not what is parseable.
